newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank vows to keep markets stable.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank vows to keep markets stable.

text.p: Taiwan central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said on Friday that the bank would keep the island's financial markets stable "at all efforts" after China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping died, the state-run Central News Agency reported.
"The central bank is closely monitoring local financial markets, it will keep the markets stable at all efforts," the agency quoted Sheu as saying.
"It will take countermeasures if necessary," he said without elaboration.
Sheu added the movements of Taiwan's financial markets had been "normal" in recent days.
Deng died late on Wednesday of complications from Parkinson's disease and a lung infection in Beijing.
The island's usually super-sensitive stock market has shrugged off political fears, rising 0.28 percent on Thursday and up 1.47 percent on Friday.
The Taiwan dollar also rebounded to T$27.595 against one U.S. dollar in Friday afternoon trade, compared with Thursday's T$27.625 close.
The central bank is capable of stabilising the financial markets, Sheu said.
